approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. A bounded score-ranked population supplies parents for connected-fragment crossover and local mutations, including its retained aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity admission precedes the surplus candidate pool. A Gaussian process trained on the complete earlier accepted archive uses integer counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity to predict the pool jointly. Each batch position takes the remaining maximizer of a fresh correlated posterior draw. Accepted offspring update both the full prediction archive and the breeding population, so allocation affects later chemistry as well as the current evaluations.
approach.novelty: Remove only the dependence between candidates' random allocation residuals while preserving every candidate's fitted mean and sampled marginal variance. Each candidate receives an independent Gaussian excursion of its existing size before the same masked maximization. The earlier mean-only sibling removed exploration altogether and scored worse; pending-mean conditioning also changed marginal variances, while shared-panel siblings changed the batch objective. None isolated cross-candidate dependence with marginal exploration held fixed. This contribution test asks whether the Parent can retain its performance without that dependence. It does not predict improved calibration or a computational speedup, and its result will concern the complete subsequent feedback loop.

observed_bottleneck: The targeted behavior is the Parent's sharing of random allocation residuals across molecular alternatives through the full conditional covariance. That dependence changes which molecules can win, while its contribution remains inseparable from marginal exploration in existing scored evidence. The actual summaries and run logs for n-559d25e9c9c7 show all supplied replicas completed, macro mean 0.574343936523512 and population SD 0.012316775530180069, with 624 strict best-generating-parent beats among 4350 scored offspring. Its confirmed count-posterior result improved macro score by 0.022573281535690642 against its own Parent, but nominal latent interval coverage is only 76.9195 percent. This motivates testing the reliance on covariance structure without assuming that poor marginal coverage proves incorrect correlations. The scored mean-only sibling n-852bc7be4d7c fell by 0.040407162268268314 in macro mean and narrowed same-pool core coverage: its result supports retaining sampled exploration, rather than repeating its complete removal. Pending-mean conditioning in n-521f362b3777 changed 287 batches and contracted selected marginal variance by 3.30 percent on average, but missed its positive score target. Shared-panel and antithetic batch-maximum siblings n-9c0f6fa601f8 and n-0db88abff519 also changed allocation without reaching their positive endpoint targets; those experiments altered coordination or objectives, not dependence alone. A new passive reconstruction of all 435 actual Parent fits reproduces all 4350 choices with maximum draw error 1.17e-13. There are nonzero off-diagonal opportunities in all pools: 5528444 of 5533200 upper-triangle covariances exceed 1e-12 in magnitude, although mean absolute pool correlation is only 0.0382386755. Using the identical logged standard normals with independent residuals at unchanged jittered marginal variance changes 420 batch sets and 2004 selection positions; 1738 choices differ under the identical Parent masks, all with unique alternative maxima. Marginal variance agreement is within 4.44e-16. On those fixed pools, mean prediction changes from 0.408111329 to 0.408273867, original SD exposure from 0.042763454 to 0.042941229, and nonempty Murcko-core coverage from 6.981609 to 6.995402 per batch. Thus a substantial dependence-specific decision opportunity exists with nearly preserved aggregate exploration exposure. These alternate molecules have no counterfactual oracle labels; the audit establishes opportunity, not score equivalence.
hypothesis: Remove cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by sampling independent Gaussian residuals with the Parent's unchanged jittered marginal variances, while retaining the fitted count-based joint posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Independent residuals changed allocation, but a timeout leaves final non-inferiority unresolved.
finding_summary.insights:
Small average model correlations can still have a large effect on who wins a sampled maximum. All recorded pools offered a covariance-removal opportunity, and almost every batch set changed even though every candidate retained the same fitted mean and sampled marginal variance on fixed inputs. Removing stochastic dependence also did not make the selected chemistry independent: on the child's same pools, actual selected-pair absolute model correlation is 0.05568 versus 0.05137 under correlated replay, and mean nonempty core coverage is 6.64 versus 6.77. Independence of allocation noise is therefore neither a scaffold-diversity constraint nor removal of the fitted joint model.

The completed seeds leave the narrower dependence-removal hypothesis plausible, but the timeout and mixed task outcomes prevent calling dependence dispensable. The retained full factorization succeeds at its first jitter in every recorded batch. The timed-out stream ends after a complete allocation and emission, with ten externally scored molecules lacking candidate feedback. Its measured fitting time is only 0.46 seconds across twenty fits; the records do not isolate the source of the long task wall time. The parent already needed about 3,265 seconds on that same task and seed, so the evidence does not establish a new covariance-factorization failure or a speed benefit from this change.

The molecular assessment explains why additional local parent beats do not settle chemical progress. Familiar aromatic, amide and amine families still coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, repeated large assemblies and constrained closures. In matched windows, molecules containing rings of at most four atoms increase from 268 to 920, and products exceeding sixty heavy atoms increase from 168 to 320. Both panels leave every detected tetrahedral centre unassigned. These are observed coverage and plausibility limits; they neither explain the timeout uniquely nor prove that removing a particular bond or scaffold would improve scores.
finding_summary.results:
Allocation cross-covariance was removed in all 426 recorded child batches while each jittered marginal variance was preserved. All recorded draws and all 4,260 masked winners reconstruct from the original normals. Replaying correlated draws on the same child pools changes 1,962 selection positions and 411 of 426 batch sets. The other fifteen sets coincide despite changed draw values; they are downstream non-effects, not failed covariance removal. Initial pools, predicted means, raw standard deviations and normal arrays match the parent exactly in all fifteen sessions.

Fourteen task runs finished. Deco-hop seed 0 timed out after 210 of 300 evaluations, so that seed has no final macro score and the full three-seed non-inferiority test cannot be decided. The two complete seeds improve by +0.011662 and +0.013814: their mean final Top-1 is 0.580592 versus 0.567854 for the same parent seeds. These two successful replicas cannot replace the missing result; the incomplete seed already loses 0.084067 on its completed sitagliptin task. Across the fourteen completed task pairs, mean recorded AUC falls from 0.474455 to 0.441510.

In matched available evaluation windows containing 4,260 scored offspring per panel, strict beats of the best generating parent rise from 615 to 690, and incumbent improvements rise from 238 to 272. Mean offspring-minus-best-parent score is still negative, changing from -0.085277 to -0.072497. The session-averaged accepted batch maximum falls from 0.487030 to 0.456226. Distinct nonempty cores fall from 1,778 to 1,711, while the largest core occupies an average 61.3% of each session's top ten proposals, versus 57.3% before. Prediction MSE falls from 0.011505 to 0.009159, but nominal 95% latent-interval coverage also falls, from 76.74% to 74.20%. These describe changed evaluated streams, not repaired calibration or scores for unselected alternatives.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring-rich families retain reactive heteroatom bonds, constrained closures and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The generator produces substantial aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry: compact aryl amides, linked aza-aromatics, aryl-containing amines, bridged lactams and fluorinated fused heterocyclic diones. Across the supplied proposal sets, ring-closure-string rates range from 0.9655 to 0.9828 and aromatic-atom-string rates from 0.9609 to 0.9769. These are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not fractions of atoms or measures of useful scaffold diversity. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout; neutral SMILES nevertheless include readily recognizable basic amines. Different seeds reach different families, but high-scoring excerpts often concentrate on closely related substitutions of a retained scaffold. Chemical plausibility is mixed: conventional amine and amide skeletons coexist with N-halogen and N-S bonds, cyanate esters, peroxide-linked repeated assemblies, cumulenes, acyl halides, unusual sulfur valence patterns and difficult ring closures. The Parent shows many of the same limitations. Neither score increases nor valid molecular graphs establish stability, synthesis, geometry or biological activity. Heavy-atom counts and ring descriptions below were read with RDKit from the supplied trajectory SMILES; numerical scores and text-counter rates come from the supplied records. All five objectives have trajectories. Coverage is incomplete for deco_hop seed 0, which stops at evaluation 210: that task has 810 recorded molecules and 780 optimizer proposals, while each other task has 900 and 870. The digest final-molecule excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not final incumbents for every seed. Comparisons involving the partial stream describe only the available chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecule has 24 heavy atoms and a fused bicyclic aza-aromatic core attached through a carboxamide to pyridyl: methoxy and methyl substituents decorate the core, and the amide nitrogen also bears terminal sulfur. Its perceived rings are three six-membered aromatic rings. Other seeds retain more indole-like aryl-amide families with N-halogen substitutions. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.6, with ring-closure and aromatic-string rates of 0.9678 and 0.9644. The conventional heteroaryl-amide framework is synthetically recognizable; its unusual nitrogen substitution is the main chemical concern. The Parent similarly explored compact indole/aza-ring amides with N-halogen or N-S bonds. The Child seed-2 best score is 0.5047376048386725 versus the Parent seed-2 best 0.4484138510190879, accompanying a different fused-ring arrangement rather than removal of those bond liabilities.
liabilities: The leading amide contains an N-S bond to terminal sulfur; other high scorers are N-chloro or N-bromo amides. These are chemically distinct from ordinary stable N-alkyl amides.
Halogen-string incidence is 0.9264, including examples with benzylic halides or N-halogen bonds; it cannot be read as predominantly benign aromatic halogen substitution.
The highest-scoring excerpt is planar and strongly scaffold-concentrated, while some late closures add constrained topology without a corresponding high score.
missing_features: Broader compact aza-aromatic amide arrangements are poorly represented in the best excerpt: the favorable nitrogen-position variants remain variations of the same substituted fused-ring family.
Conventional, stable nitrogen substitution reproducing the favorable compact amide arrangement is missing from the leading excerpt; whether such replacements preserve its score remains unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The compact methoxy/dimethyl aza-aromatic amide reaches 0.5047376048386725; related nitrogen-position variants score 0.49356871262936075. In contrast, methane, chloramine and the other tiny digest fragments score 0.0. The late molecule with a methylene inserted between carbonyl and N-chloro aniline scores 0.33864186950998887. The observed gradient favors a particular compact ring-linked carbonyl/heteroatom arrangement over isolated fragments and many altered linkages. It also tolerates N-S, N-Cl and N-Br substitutions, so the gradient supplies no evidence of a stability preference.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 family comprises a fused aza-aromatic/lactone system linked through a diazine to substituted pyridine. The best molecule has 39 heavy atoms, four six-membered rings, a carbon-linked nitrile, two O-linked cyanate groups, and vinyl, methyl and butyl substituents. Other trajectories are much larger: partial seed 0 contains repeated fused nitrogen-heterocyclic diones joined through oxygen-rich links including O-O bonds; seed 2 ends with dense polycycles bearing thiones, thiocarbamate-like groups and extended unsaturated chains. Mean proposal SMILES length is 109.5 and the maximum is 224; ring-closure and aromatic-string rates are both 0.9769. The seed-1 leader is chemically more manageable than these repeated assemblies, although its cyanates remain unusual. Compared with the Parent, seed 1 reaches 0.6501944061206573 with a 39-heavy-atom leader, versus 0.6199818405862896 with a 43-heavy-atom leader. Seed 2 instead expands from a Parent 30-heavy-atom leader at 0.616992140985949 to a 59-heavy-atom leader at 0.5946164001760306. The partial seed-0 record is not a matched final endpoint.
liabilities: O-linked cyanates are not ordinary carbon-linked nitriles; the leading molecules contain both types of group and should not be described simply as benign nitrile-rich heteroaromatics.
The partial seed-0 trajectory contains peroxide links and repeated large ring assemblies; these are observations from the full supplied trajectory, without claiming an incidence from the digest.

The cited late seed-2 molecule combines cumulated double bonds, an acyl chloride, sulfur-containing carbonyl analogues and constrained ring closures. Its dense assembly creates stability and synthetic-access concerns.
Formal valence and ring closure do not establish a feasible conformation or synthetic route for the large bridged structures.
missing_features: Compact, nonrepeating arrangements of the favorable heteroaromatic and carbonyl functions are not reached consistently across seeds; substantial output remains attached to duplicated or densely closed assemblies.

Conventional substituent alternatives preserving the successful ring arrangement are insufficiently represented among the leaders to separate useful polar-group placement from unusual cyanate chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small acyclic molecules, including bromine and an alkynyl nitrile, share the 0.5 floor. The initial aromatic lactone/nitrile assembly scores 0.5418375031378128; the linked aza-aromatic leaders reach 0.6496052966641201 and 0.6501944061206573. These observations support the combined arrangement of aromatic rings, heteroatoms and substituents, rather than a nitrile fragment alone. Adding the second cyanate in the cited close pair changes the score only from 0.6496052966641201 to 0.6501944061206573. Vinyl and propenyl variants share 0.6496052966641201. Late, much larger seed-2 molecules remain around the cited 0.5924778339212509 to 0.5946164001760306 values, providing no evidence that continued assembly growth is beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring molecules already contain basic amine chemistry. The best seed-1 molecule has 27 heavy atoms, an aminoethyl-substituted fluorophenyl ring, a benzylic bromide and a tertiary amine in a bridged ether-containing cage. Its perceived rings include a four-membered ring and a seven-membered ring. Seed 0 instead produces more conventional diaryl alkylamine chains with phenol/methoxy, aniline and halogen substituents; its cited 30-heavy-atom leader scores 0.9925994233149407. Seed 2 retains a constrained polycyclic amine joined to an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur-oxo environment. Mean proposal SMILES length is 55.9; ring-closure, aromatic-string and halogen-string rates are 0.9782, 0.9759 and 0.9885. The Parent also reached aryl-containing basic amines: the same-seed best recorded scores are 0.9959491085611949, 0.9964552366323939 and 0.9912887882944748, compared with Child values 0.9925994233149407, 0.9999918646258837 and 0.9778949666828435. The conventional seed-0 skeleton coexists with more problematic cage and sulfur chemistry in other seeds.
liabilities: The best cage combines constrained connectivity with an electrophilic benzylic bromide and unspecified stereochemistry; a high score does not establish a makeable or isolable stereoisomer.
The late seed-2 molecules use unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur-oxo connectivities and small ring closures, which require more scrutiny than an ordinary sulfonamide label would suggest.
Some successful flexible molecules have several amine centres and long hydrophobic linkers; their score alone does not characterize ionization, solubility or selectivity.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified presentations of the successful aryl/basic-amine arrangements are absent: the best cage has unassigned tetrahedral centres and no proposal has a stereocentre marker.

Credible ring geometry and stable substituent choices are not consistently coupled to the favorable amine/aromatic arrangement. Basic nitrogen itself is already present and should not be described as missing.
The neutral SMILES do not resolve which protonation state was chemically relevant; the charge-string rate alone cannot establish absence of protonatable centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-sulfonyl cyclic amine in the worst excerpt scores 0.00017210440419041065, while the aryl-containing free-amine leaders reach 0.9925994233149407 and 0.9999918646258837. The initial acid/amide/sulfonamide-rich molecules also score poorly. The observed association is with accessible aliphatic amine centres presented alongside hydrophobic aromatic groups, not merely nitrogen count or aromaticity. Both flexible chains and rigid cages can score highly in this sample, so the near-ceiling cage score does not establish a requirement for its strained topology or benzylic bromide. These are benchmark scores, not evidence of measured receptor binding.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules are propyl/ethoxy-substituted aryl systems attached to pyrazole-like or partially saturated fused nitrogen rings and N-methyl lactams. The leading molecule has 34 heavy atoms and a densely bridged ring system with perceived seven- and eight-membered rings as well as aromatic rings; an ethoxy-substituted fused cyclic ether forms another part of the structure. Near leaders rearrange the same aryl/ether/N-carbonyl components into partially saturated rings and N-N-containing variants. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.7, with ring-closure and aromatic-string rates of 0.9828 and 0.9701. The familiar aryl, ether and lactam functions give some medicinal-chemistry resemblance, but their complicated closures make synthesis uncertain. The Parent already explored related medium-ring and bridged carbonyl/nitrogen systems. Its seed-1 best is 0.24321515648721753, compared with the Child seed-1 best 0.23224471807781472; the Child does not show a new chemically independent high-scoring family.
liabilities: The leading and near-leading structures contain complex medium-ring bridges, and one near leader includes a four-membered ring. Ring richness here does not demonstrate easy synthesis or accessible conformations.
Unspecified stereocentres accompany some dense closures; the digest stereocentre-string rate is 0.0.
Late variants introduce an acyl fluoride, N-S substitution or N-O substitution while staying near the existing score range, adding chemical concerns without evidence of a distinct successful family.
missing_features: Alternative, independently organized presentations of the favorable aryl, ether and nitrogen-carbonyl combination are scarce in the leading excerpt; most changes rearrange a shared dense ring family.
Stereochemically and conformationally specified versions of the bridged structures are absent, leaving the actual spatial presentation of the retained functions unresolved.

Simpler synthetic connectivities preserving that combined functional-group arrangement are not demonstrated by the leading excerpt; their potential score cannot be inferred from the low scores of isolated fragments.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused heterocyclic dione with aryl substituents scores 0.1678386594791329. Retaining substituted aromatic regions while reorganizing nitrogen/carbonyl-containing rings gives the leading 0.23224471807781472 and 0.23063280200722125 structures. Methane and acetylene score 0.0, and the late isolated oxetane scores only 0.029488391230979422. Thus a small ring or amide fragment alone is insufficient: higher scores are associated with a larger combined aryl/ether/nitrogen-carbonyl arrangement. Similar complex variants occupy a narrow score interval, so the records do not identify an absent exact pharmacophore or establish that adding more closures is useful.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family is a compact fused nitrogen-heterocyclic dione bearing an aryl or cyclopentadienol substituent and fluorinated nitrogen-containing arms. The best molecule has 27 heavy atoms and three perceived rings: its methyl-substituted cyclopentadienol is attached to the fused heterocycle, which carries two aminomethyl arms whose nitrogens are each bonded to two fluorines. The close phenolic aromatic analogue has 28 heavy atoms. These are N-F bonds, not fluorines placed exclusively on carbon. Other seeds retain related dione/imino heterocycles with fused bridges or small unsaturated rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 48.8, with ring-closure and aromatic-string rates of 0.9655 and 0.9609. The Parent already produced fluorinated versions of the same broad family, including N-fluorinated ring nitrogens. Child seed-2 best is 0.6600793564920664 versus Parent seed-2 best 0.6025252354500499, whereas Child seed-0 best is 0.5669542627486331 versus Parent seed-0 best 0.6510211907030741. The more successful seed-2 chemistry still retains unusual fluorinated nitrogen.
liabilities: Repeated N,N-difluoroamine groups and other N-fluoro variants are conspicuous stability/reactivity concerns. Their presence cannot be summarized as ordinary medicinal fluorination.
Some variants add N-N bonds, imino groups or constrained unsaturated rings. The chemical structures require interpretation beyond valence sanitization.
The largest repeated structures are both chemically cumbersome and extremely low scoring, while late local variants can retain questionable bonds despite large score changes.
missing_features: Stable conventional ways to combine the favorable intermediate size, heterocyclic carbonyl groups and fluorinated substituents are not demonstrated among the strongest examples; replacing N-F bonds may alter the score and has no established benefit here.
The best partially saturated ring has unassigned stereochemistry, and its enolic representation leaves tautomeric and conformational identity insufficiently characterized.
The best excerpt remains concentrated on a shared fused dione family; chemically distinct frameworks with a comparable arrangement of polar and hydrophobic regions are not demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial larger aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The compact phenolic and cyclopentadienol analogues carrying repeated difluorinated nitrogen arms score 0.6507833193658838 and 0.6600793564920664. In a close late analogue, replacing one difluorinated aminomethyl arm by a fluoroethyl arm gives 0.5091165870780078; replacing the other aminomethyl arm directly by fluorine gives 0.22937302745794097. The observed gradient therefore distinguishes how fluorine and nitrogen are arranged on the compact dione scaffold, rather than rewarding any fluorine-containing molecule. The very large repeated assembly scores 3.719100443911319e-42, while isolated fluorine scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Both extremes fail in the supplied records. The high scores of N-F-rich structures provide no evidence that the objective enforces ordinary stability or synthetic plausibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading molecules contain N-S, N-Cl, N-Br or repeated N-F bonds; other supplied output includes O-O links, cyanate esters and a final molecule combining an acyl chloride with cumulated double bonds. These concerns occur within substantial ring systems, so absence of rings is not the problem.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically ordinary bond environments when it builds otherwise recognizable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic bond-environment awareness could distinguish stable substituent placement from reactive heteroatom bonds while retaining independently learned favorable scaffold features. Such chemistry constraints need their own evaluation; the supplied scores do not show that deleting every unusual group would improve reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The best aryl-amine cage includes a four-membered ring, while other leading structures combine medium-ring bridges with dense fused systems. Late large assemblies contain additional constrained aromatic closures. High ring-closure rates establish abundant connectivity, not accessible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can close rings but does not demonstrate control over the geometric and synthetic feasibility of the resulting bridges.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposal generation would need to distinguish ordinary feasible rings from arbitrary closures using local ring topology and accessible geometry, without assuming every small ring is invalid or every additional ring is useful. This property can be evaluated independently of hidden objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest task reports a stereocentre-string rate of 0.0. Parsed leading cage amines, bridged lactams and a partially saturated enol-containing ring have unassigned tetrahedral centres. Neutral charge strings also leave the protonation choices of basic amines unspecified, although those centres are present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical definition even after creating tetrahedral centres in successful scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and proposal process would need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when topology creates it. Protonation and tautomer choices should be treated as separate chemical-state questions; neither missing charge markers nor unspecified stereochemistry proves a score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set has mean SMILES length 109.5 and maximum length 224, with repeated heterocyclic assemblies in the full trajectories. Its leading compact linked-ring molecule has 39 heavy atoms, while a supplied late molecule has 58. Elsewhere a repeated large dione assembly is the lowest-scoring cited molecule, so size growth is not uniformly rewarded.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently limit repeated scaffold assembly or find compact versions of useful functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs ways to retain favorable groups while changing attachment or reducing redundant assembly, rather than relying on further duplication. The trajectories support evaluating structural complexity and compact alternatives; they do not justify a universal size cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading excerpts recur as substituted aryl amides, linked aza-aromatics, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems or fluorinated fused diones. Multiple ring-position, side-chain or heteroatom substitutions can preserve similar scores without demonstrating a chemically independent family; other seeds nevertheless show that alternative families can occur.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring chemistry is often confined to close variants of one scaffold within a seed, despite abundant rings and many distinct SMILES.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need scaffold-level transformations that reorganize learned functional-group relationships while retaining chemical plausibility. Useful diversity should be judged by distinct makeable frameworks and scored descendants, not only identity counts or ring-closure strings.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
